page: The UpCloud STARTER-4xCPU-16GB is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9575F processor operating at 2.0 GHz, providing 4 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with a shared CPU allocation. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core, alongside 50 GB of local SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks reveal strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression scoring in the top 25%. Multi-core performance, including Geekbench multi-core and stress-ng multi-core tests, falls within the average range. However, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is poor, scoring in the bottom 10%, and Passmark memory and physics tests show weaker performance in the bottom 25%.

Given its shared CPU allocation and starter classification, this server offers a cost-effective option for workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated CPU resources. It is suitable for general-purpose applications, static web serving, software compilation, and basic database operations, but is less optimal for memory-intensive tasks or heavy multi-threaded physics simulations.
